headline: Acquisitions lift sales, margins narrow on mix shift
summary_short: Net sales were $977.9M, up 56% y/y (+15% organic) largely on the Micromax and EFC acquisitions and pass-through metals pricing, while gross margin fell 840bps to 34.2% and diluted EPS rose to $0.32 from $0.20 y/y.
summary_long: Net sales rose 56% y/y to $977.9M (15% organic), driven by the Micromax and EFC acquisitions plus $317M of pass-through metals pricing in Electronics. Gross margin fell 840bps to 34.2% on a lower-margin, metals-heavier product mix and Specialties raw-material inflation; ex-metals margin was down only 240bps. Operating profit rose 21% to $113.7M despite a 28% rise in opex from acquisition integration and incentive-comp costs. Net income rose 63% to $77.3M; diluted EPS rose to $0.32 from $0.20. Cash fell to $189.6M from $626.5M, mainly funding $866M of acquisitions. Element Solutions guides FY2026 capex to ~$100M, and on July 6, 2026 agreed to be acquired by Solstice for 0.5 shares plus $10.00 cash per ESI share, closing H1 2027.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven primarily by the Micromax and EFC acquisitions completed in Q1 2026 plus higher pass-through precious-metals pricing in Electronics; organic growth was a more modest 15%.

Subsequent event: on July 6, 2026 Element Solutions agreed to be acquired by Solstice Advanced Materials for 0.5 Solstice shares plus $10.00 cash per ESI share, expected to close in H1 2027 — unrelated to Q2 operating results.

Reported net sales growth of 56% (organic +15%) reflected the Micromax and EFC acquisitions and $317M of pass-through metals pricing in the Assembly Solutions business, per the release's segment discussion.

Gross profit dollars grew on volume and M&A, but margin fell 840bps to 34.2% (only -240bps ex pass-through metals) on a lower-margin, metals-heavier Electronics mix and Specialties raw-material inflation.

Operating profit rose 21% as revenue growth outpaced a 28% rise in opex, which included $10.3M of costs from the newly acquired Micromax and EFC businesses, higher incentive compensation, and acquisition-integration costs.

EBIT rose more than operating income because it captures net foreign-exchange gains of $6.7M (vs a $17.1M loss a year ago) and other income including metals-derivative gains, both below operating profit on the income statement.
Net income rose 63% as revenue growth and a swing to a $6.7M FX gain (vs a $17.1M loss a year ago) offset $11.1M of higher interest expense from new term-loan debt and a higher tax rate.
Diluted EPS growth of 60% closely tracked net income's 63% rise since diluted share count was roughly flat y/y (243.9M vs 242.2M, +0.7%).
